meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why am I here, Hale, and why did my son find out about a zero from his phone?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What was the basis for it?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
Students draft elsewhere and paste it in. Who else has seen this history, and was Owen shown it before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Did you speak to Owen before November 3? Yes or no.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote. It's a mistake, not proof of anything. And you still haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen first.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. Then whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. And Hale, I asked you a yes-or-no question twice.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Outlines change. Revising an argument is what you teach them to do.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. A private rewrite, to put this behind him, not because he did anything. In writing tonight, the zero removed, and nothing on his record.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. I'll confirm it with Owen tonight, so put the date in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay on Thursday the twelfth after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require written confirmation that the zero is removed, and an answer to whether you spoke with Owen before November 3. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants that in writing tonight along with an answer on whether you spoke to Owen first. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You showed the invented line in the play itself, because she could check it with her own eyes and your answer to her misquote defence closed the gap.
What cost ground: You never answered whether you spoke to Owen before the zero, even after she asked twice, which kept her suspicious that you punished first and asked later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the essay appearing at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, landed very close to that night. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether you spoke to Owen before November 3, answer yes or no straight away, before moving on to the version history.
